evidence.source_text_exact: Permanent facilities must follow Chapter 2 of this UFC, which contains modifications to the International Building Code® (IBC).
Buildings and facilities are considered permanent construction unless they meet other definitions herein.
Permanent construction is intended to address a level of quality and durability to achieve a life expectancy of more than 25 years.

evidence.source_text_exact: Temporary construction includes structures erected for a period less than 180 days both inside and outside the United States its territories and possessions.

Temporary structures must conform to the structural strength, fire safety, means of egress, accessibility, light, ventilation, and sanitary requirements of the IBC Section 3103, as modified in Chapter 2 of this UFC.
Extension of temporary construction occupancy or usage 180 days or beyond requires a written justification request and approval from the BO/AHJ.

Extension approvals may be renewed at the discretion of the Building Official / Authority Having Jurisdiction (BO/AHJ); however, occupancy or facility usage cannot occur beyond 5 years from date of initial occupancy.
Further extension may be granted where a longer construction plan is justified, and an AHJ-approved end-of-use date has been established for the temporary facility.

pilot_review.review_focus: Compare with Temporary construction level in UFC 1-201-01. Keep the initial period, approval conditions, and further-extension text together; different source scopes are not automatically a contradiction.
